messages:
Maya Chen: Quick update — brought up strato-6b (8k context) in int4 and int8, ran microbench vs our prod 7b baseline.
Jon Patel: awesome. where are the numbers? :eyes:
Maya Chen: p50/p95 latency (batch=1):  int8=85ms/220ms, int4=78ms/200ms, prod-7b=int8=65ms/170ms
Samir Rao: so int4 is slightly faster but not by much. what about throughput and token cost?
Maya Chen: throughput (tokens/sec single stream): int8=85 t/s, int4=95 t/s, 7b=110 t/s. unit compute cost estimates (per 1M tokens): int8=$5.4, int4=$3.9, 7b=$6.8
Anna Lopez: where'd cost numbers come from? infra or extrapolated?
Maya Chen: extrapolated from bench GPU-hours using our reserved cost model + perf kernels. included prefix cache hit 0.12 baseline.
bench-bot: full bench artifacts uploaded: https://redwood-internal/snapshots/strato-6b/bench-1976123456
Jon Patel: how's quality? any regressions on our eval suite?
Maya Chen: eval-lift on LlamaBench-like suite: int8 = baseline (delta Rouge/EM within ±0.5), int4 = -1.8 average on QA F1, larger drop on instruction-following (~-2.4). Short prompts (<=40 tokens) similar; regressions show up on long-context reasoning.
Samir Rao: that's interesting — int4 hurt multi-step reasoning. any hallucination uptick?
Maya Chen: slight increase in factual hallucinations (precision down ~1.2 points). Not catastrophic, but noticeable on customer-facing tasks.
Anna Lopez: product asks for recommendation for GTN: is this a candidate for routing/cheapest-tier?
Jon Patel: tradeoffs look like: int4 = best unit cost, reasonable latency for high-volume non-critical tasks; int8 = middle ground; keep 7b for latency-sensitive or quality-critical.
Maya Chen: my proposal:
- Default serving: strato-6b-int8 for most routes (stable quality, ~15% cost savings vs 7b).
- Heavy-volume low-criticality bursts: route to int4 with automated quality sampling and fallback to int8 on failures.
- Keep prod-7b as premium route for shortest-latency, highest-quality flows.
Samir Rao: add canary: 5% traffic to int4 with eval hooks and degrade threshold @ -2.0 F1 -> auto rollback to int8.
Anna Lopez: will GTN care about per-token billing delta? They want clear dollar delta to show to customers.
Maya Chen: included a simple calc in the bench artifact: estimated monthly cost for 500M tokens/month — int4=$1.95k, int8=$2.7k, 7b=$3.4k (in reserved pricing). Savings vs 7b: int4 ~43%, int8 ~21%.
Jon Patel: nice. any perf tuning steps to reduce int4 quality loss?
Maya Chen: next actions: (1) run quant-aware calibration with larger calibration set, (2) test hybrid quant (KV-cache int8 + compute int4), (3) rerun eval including longer reasoning prompts.
bench-bot: scheduled follow-up run: 1976200000 (hybrid tests)
Samir Rao: ok, sounds actionable. I'll draft the routing policy + rollout playbook and drop in /docs.
Anna Lopez: thanks Maya. can you paste the eval summary table here when available? :thumbsup:
Maya Chen: will do. putting the core numbers into the ticket now -> https://redwood-internal/issue/ML-1983
